# Dekker's product: TwoProd without an FMA

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `two_prod_dekker` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

An approximation $p + e$ of $a b$:

$$p + e \approx a b.$$

## C++

No public operation computes this kernel on its own. It replaces [`two_prod`](two_prod.md) in constant evaluation, where there is no fused multiply-add.

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $p = \mathrm{RN}(a b)$.
- $\lvert p + e - a b\rvert \le \tfrac{13}{8}\,\eta$.
- $p + e = a b$ exactly, when $a b = 0$ or $\lvert a b\rvert \ge \eta/(2u^2)$.

The constants of the bound, for each limb type, from `gen/claims.json`:

| | `double` | `float` |
|---|---|---|
| unit roundoff $u$ | $2^{-53}$ | $2^{-24}$ |
| absolute term $t\,\eta$ | $13 \cdot 2^{-1077} \approx 8.0286 \times 10^{-324}$ | $13 \cdot 2^{-152} \approx 2.2771 \times 10^{-45}$ |
| `unit`, `tiny`, as compiled | `0.0`, `0x1p-1073` | `0.0f`, `0x1p-148f` |
| `unit_computed`, `tiny_computed` | `0.0`, `0x1p-1073` | `0.0f`, `0x1p-148f` |

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 4 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `two_prod_dekker_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/TwoProdDekker.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/TwoProdDekker.v), against `two_prod_dekker_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); `make -C proofs` finds no axiom in its proof beyond the four allowed ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition two_prod_dekker_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (4 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall a b : R,
  fmt emin prec a ->
  fmt emin prec b ->
  let '(p, e) := two_prod_dekker emin prec tie_even a b in
  fmt emin prec p /\
  fmt emin prec e /\
  p = RN emin prec (a * b) /\
  Rabs ((p + e) - (a * b)) <= (13 / 8) * eta emin /\
  (((a * b) = 0 \/ bpow radix2 (2 * prec - 1) * eta emin <= Rabs (a * b)) -> (p + e) = (a * b)).
```

## Source

**Algorithm:** Dekker's product with Veltkamp's split (Dekker 1971); overflow preconditions [BM11](../developer/design/phase0/references.md#bm11). **License:** algorithm: published; proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/two_prod_dekker.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/two_prod_dekker.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/Model.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`split`](split.md).

```
# Dekker's product: TwoProd without an FMA, the constant-evaluation variant of two_prod. It requires
# that no intermediate overflows. The underflow term (13/8) eta is the proved one (the source has
# 7/2); exhaustive runs on toy formats approach it.

(ah, al) = split(a)
(bh, bl) = split(b)
p  = prod(a, b)
q0 = prod(ah, bh)
t1 = sub(q0, p)
q1 = prod(ah, bl)
t2 = add(t1, q1)
q2 = prod(al, bh)
t3 = add(t2, q2)
q3 = prod(al, bl)
e  = add(t3, q3)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone1/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone1/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone1.md#two_prod_dekker)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.

| Run | Cases judged | Failed | largest error / bound (always) | largest error / bound (when product large) | Bound attained |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 40 runners on 3 machines | 58 648 440 | 0 | 0.921384 | 0 (exact) | no |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 40 runners on 3 machines | 55 122 824 | 0 | 0.929436 | 0 (exact) | no |
| toy formats, every operand: 6 domains of 6 formats (1 stopped before the end: see below) | 3 330 757 | 0 | 0.943510 (`fp:7:-12:-1`) | 0 (exact) | no |

A finding of the run on linux-x86-64, the interpreter on `fp:7:-20:-6`: the interpreter exited with 2; stream error: line 1: stream ended before the generator's trailer: the runner stopped early or the stream was truncated.

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: what is proved and what is not written yet there is in [What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values).
